"My advice is, if you get involved? Watch your back. Mind yourself. Don't trust her."

He looks away, thinking. His hands held together in front of his mouth, not quite the form of Luddic prayer.

"Seen a few fleet operators fall right off the map. She's looking for something. Big risk. I'd bet if I knew what it was I'd say it wasn't worth it."

"My advice is don't get involved. And you're not going to listen, are you."

He looks away, thinking. His hands held together in front of his mouth, not quite the form of Luddic prayer.

"Seen a few fleet operators fall right off the map. She's looking for something. Big risk. I'd bet if I knew what it was I'd say it wasn't worth it."

His eyes meet yours through the link.

"We won't. I'm going to be rich, get richer, and enjoy my splendid home. You can go do something very stupid if you have to. Just hope it doesn't get us all killed."

His eyes meet yours through the link.

"I'm going to be rich, get richer, and enjoy my splendid home. You should do the same."

He looks away again, presumably at achingly beautiful mountain vistas. "But you won't."

His eyes meet yours through the link.

"That sounds like the third worst idea I've ever heard."

He falls back in his chair with an unhappy sound.

"Not now."

He leans back in his chair.

"Sure."

Your comms are routed through a secretary, either a holosim or product of uncanny cosmetic and behavior tuning, then, after a brief wait, the link blinks to Director Glamor-Rotanev.

"Captain $playerLastName," she says with diminishing breeziness.

The Director's face creates a smile. "He wasn't supposed to tell anyone. But this is Cornelius Elek, so I cannot be surprised."

Her face, and tone, go blank again.

"You have something more to say about Elek. Proceed."
"Oh?" The Director's face is immobile.
"What made you think that, I wonder," she says.

Glamor-Rotanev creates a smile for you.

"Yes, I was admiring your new acquisition." Her eyes flicker oddly, and you detect what might be a rare spark of genuine amusement. 

"Or perhaps I should call it your very, very old acquisition."

Glamor-Rotanev creates a smile for you.

"And you found it." She sounds unsurprised by the news. "Elek was distraught, I am to understand."

Her eyes flicker oddly, and you detect what might be a rare spark of genuine amusement.

Glamor-Rotanev creates a smile for you.

"And you found what he didn't know he was looking for." She sounds unsurprised. "Elek was distraught, I am to understand."

Her eyes flicker oddly, and you detect what might be a rare spark of genuine amusement.

Glamor-Rotanev creates a smile for you.

"I am a patron of the sciences. Didn't you hear?"

She nods slowly, once.

"It will take some time, and credits, for him to become a useful asset again. It is much as any investment."
"I cannot answer, as that investment has not fully matured," she says. "Which brings me to business."
"Your impulse to moralize is irrelevant to my interests," she says. "Let us return to business."
Her eyes fix upon you through the link. "And that business is the Onslaught Mk.I, which you found."

"Old records," she says curtly.

"The Galatia Academy doesn't know what it has, much less how to make good use of it. Their lack of self-motivation is self-evident."

"Then this topic serves no more purpose," she says frostily.

"Anything else?"

"I am satisfied, $playerName."

It's not that her tone is warm, more that it lacks a certain otherwise ubiquitous contempt perceivable only now by its absence. 

Presumably temporary, of course.
She makes no response.

Her eyes flicker oddly.

"You've revised your position?"

She leans back ever so slightly, but makes no outward response.

Her expression hasn't changed, but it feels somehow more impatient.

Her eyes flicker subtly, her expression more glazed and vacant than before.

"Very... good, captain," she says.

Your comms are routed through a secretary, either a holosim or product of uncanny cosmetic and behavior tuning, then, after a brief wait, the link blinks to Director Glamor-Rotanev.

"Captain $playerLastName," she says, then pauses. "You found something, didn't you."

The comms flick into an active feed nearly instantly.

"Captain," Director Glamor-Rotanev greets you, simply. "I was just admiring your new acquisition."

Her eyes flicker oddly, and you detect what might be a rare spark of genuine amusement. 

"Or perhaps it is better described as your very, very old acquisition."

"Excellent."

To your shock, her smile is nearly human. The mask is replaced almost instantly, though a slackening echo of the expression remains on her lips.

"I, and my researchers, are most eager to examine your findings. And you to be paid, no doubt."

"It pleases me to hear that." She doesn't smile.

"I, and my researchers, are most eager to examine your findings. And you to be paid, no doubt.

"Something." She raises an eyebrow.

"It was not human or AI-derived." This doesn't sound like a question.

Her eyes, previously distant, stare at you through the link for a several seconds before she replies.

"I am eager to reward you for your work." Her tone is not inviting. "CEO Sun is in full agreement. There are extraordinary discoveries and profits to be made. I am uninterested in an obstinate parody of negotiation."

"Don't act this obstinate pretense of negotiation. You $shipOrFleet has been scanned. And we knew what you found well before you arrived anyway." She pauses quite consciously.

"I am... most eager to reward your work."

Despite her words, the tone is icy. "CEO Sun is in full agreement. We may share in extraordinary discoveries and profits."
Her expression remains frozen with disdainful impatience.
"Tell me what you found."
"It was not the 'Threat'," she says. It doesn't sound like a question.

She blinks once.

"Tell me what you found."
"Fine," she says briskly.
"I am particularly interested in the hull you recovered from the Abyss. The Onslaught Mk.I is unmistakable."
"My strategic predictors tagged you with reasonable odds of success," she says. "I must congratulate their operators."
"Oh?" Her eyes give a disconcerting twitch. "I should like to examine your discoveries."
For a moment her brow develops a wrinkle. "More?" she says, and it disappears.
"I am particularly interested in the hull you recovered from the Abyss. The Onslaught Mk.I is... unmistakable."
Glamor-Rotanev gives you a frosty look.
"You've been most useful," she says ominously.

"A marvelous find, captain," the Director says softly.

"This is precisely what I have been searching for. You've been... quite essential."

Her eyes are very still, like a corpse.

"These are exceedingly useful. We shall..." She pauses.

Then creates the approximation of a smile.

"Great things shall be made, captain. You will see."
OR
"Excellent," she says placidly, eyes seemingly focused elsewhere. "This will do much to advance my initiative."
OR
Her eyes are inhumanly still.

"We shall want more. You must bring more."
OR
"I eagerly anticipate investigation of these artifacts." Her eyes twitch disconcertingly.

"These are quite... unique."

A rare smile flits on the Director's lips.

"You must find more for me, captain."

"More fascinating specimens." Her voice is dark.

"Our results have already proven to be most stimulating."
OR
"Breathtaking," the Director of Special Acquisitions says softly.

Her eyes twitch inhumanly.

She says nothing, but her eyebrow raises fractionally. It is not an invitation to continue.

Nonetheless.
"Good," she says.
"You've asked quite enough for today," she says. "Captain."

"Research and development," she says. Her expression isn't quite a smirk.

"These components are obviously derived from a neglected branch of Domain-era technology. This makes them fundamentally human technology. The path to profitable exploitation is fundamentally open, albeit complex. The Tri-Tachyon corporation is ideally placed to exploit them."

"In the simplest terms," her voice contains more than a hint of condescension, "they are autonomous self-fabricating, self-modifying constructs derived from ancient Domain designs. Their intent, so far as they could be said to have intent, is destructive toward our technological base."

"'Why' is a more difficult question."

Her dead eyes move oddly. "I find it amusing that the Luddics would recoil in horror, but they could not find a better ally to their cause."

"These are not artificial intelligences," she says decisively.

"Not that such distinction is necessary to Hegemony regulators. Whatever future war the Hegemony initiates, whatever new oppressions they conceive, it will be a consequence of leadership as paranoid as their masses are ignorant."

"Besides," she says, self-satisfied, "if I am right about everything, there will be no need for a war."

"Is a machine alive? Is a virus?" She pauses for a fraction of a second before providing her own answer.

"I don't care."

"Functionally the 'Threat' phenomenon demonstrates no attempt to present a sense of selfhood, collective or otherwise. What passes for communication is hostile and garbled; the loose ends of automatic warnings and obsolete Domain decrees. If it is conscious in any form, it is impossibly solipsistic."

"Which is just as well," the Director produces a robotic half-smile. "It will be a better tool that way."

"Research and development." 

The Director releases a deliberate breath.

"We know it isn't human. We know it is powerful. The return on investment, therefore, is beyond human imagination."

She looks satisfied with the thought.

"That is speculation for the research division. Or perhaps you would care to ask a philosopher? Or a curate?" This last idea appears to amuse her, insofar as she is capable of expressing that, or any, emotion.

"My interest is in what these specimens, these phenomena, can DO. For me. Or the Company."

She pulls her glassy eyes back to the comm-link. 

"For humanity. At least that small percentage of it willing to accept the radical and necessary future."

The link settles on feed of volatiles futures scrolling across the crest of the Tri-Tachyon corporation for just a moment before the comm-link connects you with a perfectly coiffed junior secretary.

"The Tri-Tachyon Corporation welcomes you to Eochu Bres. Their smile is uncannily bright. May we presume you wish to accept Director Glamor-Rotanev's invitation?"

"Fantastic. A priority flight path has been pre-approved for your convenience. The Tri-Tachyon Corporation is pleased to wish you a most profitable meeting with the Director of Special Acquisitions."

The uncanny smile re-appears, perfectly, once more. It's a little unsettling.

"Fantastic." The face maintains an uncanny smile. "The Director is most eager to meet you."

An apologetic - but not guilty - expression forms. "Unfortunately, the automated defenses of the Tri-Tachyon Corporation have flagged your ID as a hostile and your shuttle would be gunned down upon approach. Please contact customer service to resolve this misunderstanding."

"We hope you have a pleasant and profitable day."

The smile re-appears.
